info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package taxonomy is the product catalogue's shape: which categories exist, what each product is called, which category it sits in, what it is tagged with, and the order the two are shown in.

get.summary: Read returns the whole product catalogue: every category in display order, each carrying the products filed under it in theirs.
get.description:
Read returns the whole product catalogue: every category in display order, each
carrying the products filed under it in theirs. This is what the console's
navigation and the marketing landing page are rendered from, and it is readable
signed out — it holds no tenant data, only the same list of products every
visitor sees.

`?brand=` narrows it the way a brand's own console does: only the categories
that brand admits, and within them only the taxa scoped to it. Unpublished
taxa are served to a platform SuperAdmin alone, so the editor can see what it
has staged while nobody else can.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description:
Brand returns only what that brand's console shows — the categories it
admits, and within them the taxa scoped to it. Empty returns everything.

delete.description:
Removes one empty category. A category that still has taxa
filed under it is refused with 409 and a count: deleting the label off a group
must never silently take the products wearing it, and the alternative — orphan
rows naming a category that no longer exists — is a catalogue that cannot be
rendered. Move or delete its taxa first. An id no category holds is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the slug to act on, from the path.

put.summary: Creates or replaces one category and returns it as stored.
put.description:
Creates or replaces one category and returns it as stored. The id in
the URL is the one it is filed under whatever the body says, so a category can
never be written under a name it was not addressed by — which also makes create
and replace the same act, and is why there is no POST beside this.

Platform SuperAdmin only: one catalogue serves every tenant, so an org admin who
could rename a category would rename it for all of them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the category slug to write, from the path.

delete.summary: Removes one product from the catalogue.
delete.description:
Removes one product from the catalogue. An id no taxon holds is a
404. To take a product out of view without losing what was written about it, set
`published` to false instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the slug to act on, from the path.

put.summary: Creates or replaces one product and returns it as stored.
put.description:
Creates or replaces one product and returns it as stored. The id in the
URL is the one it is filed under whatever the body says. The category must
already exist — a taxon naming a category that does not is refused with 400
rather than stored where nothing can render it.

A taxon opens exactly one way: `route` for a product the console renders
itself, or `href` for one that genuinely lives at its own domain. Giving both,
or neither, is refused.

Platform SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the taxon slug to write, from the path.

brands.description:
Brands are the brands whose console shows this category. Absent means every
brand.

id.description: ID is the stable slug this category is addressed by, e.g. "observe".

label.description: Label is the display name, e.g. "Observe".

order.description: Order is where the category sits among its siblings, ascending.

summary.description:
Summary is the one line describing what the category groups, shown as the
header copy on its landing page.

taxa.description: Taxa are the products filed under this category, in display order.

brands.description:
Brands are the brands whose console shows this taxon. Absent means every
brand its category admits.

category.description: Category is the id of the category this taxon is filed under.

description.description: Description is the one line shown beneath the name in the catalogue and nav.

href.description:
Href is the absolute URL an external product launches, for the taxa that
genuinely live at their own domain. Empty for an in-console product.

icon.description:
Icon names the icon the surface renders, e.g. "Database". It is a NAME, not
an image: which icon set draws it is the rendering surface's business.

id.description: ID is the stable slug this taxon is addressed by, e.g. "vector".

name.description: Name is the display name, e.g. "Vector".

order.description: Order is where the taxon sits within its category, ascending.

published.description:
Published is whether the taxon is shown. An unpublished taxon is served only
to an editor, so a product can be staged before anyone sees it.

route.description:
Route is the in-console path this taxon opens, e.g. "/vector". Set for a
product the console renders itself; empty for an external one.

tags.description: Tags are free-form labels for search and grouping across categories.

categories.description: Categories are the groupings, in display order, each with its own taxa.

brands.description: Brands are the brands whose console shows it. Omit for every brand.

id.description: ID is the category slug to write, from the path.

label.description: Label is the display name. Required.

order.description: Order is where the category sits among its siblings, ascending.

summary.description: Summary is the one line describing what the category groups.

deleted.description: Deleted is the id that no longer exists.

brands.description:
Brands are the brands whose console shows it. Omit for every brand its
category admits.

category.description: Category is the id of an EXISTING category to file it under. Required.

description.description: Description is the one line shown beneath the name.

href.description:
Href is the absolute URL an external product launches. Give this or route,
never both.

icon.description: Icon names the icon the surface renders, e.g. "Database".

id.description: ID is the taxon slug to write, from the path.

name.description: Name is the display name. Required.

order.description: Order is where it sits within its category, ascending.

published.description:
Published is whether it is shown. Omitted means published — a taxon someone
took the trouble to write is meant to be seen, and hiding one is the
deliberate act.

route.description:
Route is the in-console path it opens, e.g. "/vector". Give this or href,
never both.

tags.description: Tags are free-form labels for search and grouping across categories.
